CalendarClient.list: (): Promise<CalendarEvent[]>  Stored events from the main process store. The view sorts them.
CalendarClient.importIcs: (text: string): Promise<CalendarImportResult>  Main process parses the text with electron/services/calendar.parseIcs, merges with mergeEvents, persists, and returns counts. Must enforce MAX_ICS_BYTES itself.
CalendarClient.clear: (): Promise<void>  Removes imported events only. Does not touch .ics files.

limitations: Not mounted anywhere. The shell must add the route, and the captain must supply the client through the IPC bridge. No calendar IPC channel exists yet.
Recurrence is not expanded. Repeating events are skipped and counted, and the preview says so.
Only UTC and floating times are supported. Other time zones are skipped and counted.
Floating and all-day events are grouped by the day written in the file. UTC events are grouped by local day. When a file mixes both, the order between them can differ from the real instant.
Stored events beyond the first 200 are not shown. There is no pagination, and the view says how many are hidden.
The preview shows at most 50 events. Skipped items and totals are still counted.
Import sends the same text that was previewed. The main process must parse it again and enforce the size limit, because the renderer parse is only a preview.

Tests use server-rendered markup and pure helpers. Effect-driven loading, file selection and the confirm dialog are not exercised in a DOM. The repo has no DOM test runtime, and adding one needs a dependency change this worker did not make.

Not checked in the running Electron app or with a screen reader. Accessibility coverage is markup-level only: labelled file input, aria-live status region, labelled day groups, disabled import with a stated reason.
Observation outside this worker's paths: src/ui/Dialog.tsx sets aria-labelledby to a title id that is absent while the dialog is closed. The dialog owner should check this.
No personal calendar access, accounts, OAuth or network. Nothing reads a user calendar.
